bullets.title: June NFP badly missed at 57k; Fed widely expected on hold through 2026
bullets.body: June nonfarm payrolls rose just 57k vs. ~110k consensus (prior months revised -74k cumulatively), with the unemployment rate falling to 4.2% only because labor force participation dropped 0.3pt—the 98th-percentile move. Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, and Wolfe all conclude the soft data keeps the Fed on hold through year-end; Wolfe forecasts June core CPI at -0.06% headline / 0.23% core, also dovish. Fed Chair Warsh acknowledged at Sintra that inflation risks 'have come down,' signaling no urgency to hike.

bullets.title: Meta cloud compute announcement triggers week's biggest cross-asset rotation
bullets.body: Bloomberg reported Meta is building 'Meta Compute' to sell excess AI capacity externally, sending META +9% but cratering neoclouds CRWV -14% and NBIS -17% (META is >50% and ~33% of their respective backlogs). Semis and memory sold off sharply—SOX -6.4%, Global Memory -15%—while Software/Internet rebounded. Analysts are split: bulls (Jefferies, Citi, KeyBanc) see it as capex-ROI positive with $20B+ ARR optionality; bears (Oppenheimer, DA Davidson) read it as evidence AI monetization is still elusive. The Tech Momentum factor fell ~20% MTD, worst since early 2000s.

bullets.title: Q2 2026 was historic for equities: SOX +88%, NDX +21%, EM +23%
bullets.body: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index posted its best quarter on record (+88%), driven entirely by AI capex and memory tightness. Nasdaq Composite gained 21.4% and MSCI EM rose 23.3%—best quarter since 2Q 2009. The rally was narrow: Mag 7 shed $2.3T in June alone as rotation began, while equal-weight S&P and Russell 2000 outperformed cap-weighted by ~300bp. June MSCI EM declined 1.7% as the Fed turned hawkish and the dollar strengthened.

bullets.title: Memory upcycle structurally intact: DRAM undersupplied until 2Q28, prices up 8x YoY
bullets.body: UBS raised 2H26 DDR contract pricing to +32% QoQ in 3Q26 (from +17%) and NAND to +30% QoQ, forecasting industry revenues of $992bn in 2026 and $1.76tn in 2027 with ~$1.2tn FCF. DDR5 spot hit $43.14 (+10% MoM, +740% YoY). DRAM bit demand growth of +36% in 2027 vs supply growth of only +19% creates an 'unprecedented gap.' HBM demand raised to 33.1bn Gb in 2026 (+90% YoY). SK Hynix removed price caps from long-term contracts. MU PT $1,625 (Buy).

bullets.title: AI infrastructure capex bubble debate intensifies; $748B hyperscaler obligations in focus
bullets.body: Jefferies flagged that OpenAI costs ~$14k to serve a $200 subscription, Anthropic ~$8k—making unit economics 'broken.' Hyperscalers (AMZN, MSFT, GOOGL) hold ~$748bn in remaining capex commitments tied to these unprofitable AI startups. A NY bill would impose a 1-year data center permit moratorium. JPM warns the SOX rally vs. flat hyperscalers mirrors 1999-2000 comms-equipment vs. service-provider divergence. Still, LLM token volumes surged +70% MoM in June (20x YoY) and GPU rental prices rose across all tiers, supporting the demand-exceeds-supply case.

bullets.title: Broadening trade accelerating: median S&P 1500 stock growing EPS double-digits
bullets.body: Multiple sell-side strategists (MS, Citi, JPM) note that median S&P 1500 stock is now delivering double-digit earnings growth—fastest pace since post-COVID—as operating leverage returns. Equal-weight index is outperforming cap-weighted. Earnings revisions breadth is at a 5-year high. Mag 7 and S&P 493 are both expected to deliver 17% EPS growth in 2027, the first convergence since 2021. Citi raised its S&P 500 year-end target to 8,100, based on $350/$400 EPS for 2026/27.

bullets.title: Fed hawkishness: nine FOMC members project hikes; September odds ~70%
bullets.body: The June FOMC dot plot showed nine members anticipating hikes in 2026, with six projecting two or more. Markets priced ~33bp of tightening through year-end heading into the NFP miss, which pulled July hike odds to ~17%. JPMorgan and 22V see September hike as unlikely if core PCE stays at ~0.21% MoM; above 0.25-0.30% would significantly raise odds. Chair Warsh is eliminating the dot plot and moving away from forward guidance.

bullets.title: Hedge fund de-grossing underway: gross leverage at 98th percentile, momentum -17% from peak
bullets.body: JPM Prime reports HF gross leverage peaked post-June expiry at 92nd/98th percentile (12m/5y), with early de-grossing flows in the last 3 days of June. US Momentum factor fell ~17% from June 22 peak. Info Tech/Semis were the most sold sectors globally—Asia L/S sold Tech at record pace, Japan saw largest monthly net selling on record. HFs net sold Mag 7 and Software at -2z each. Systematic L/S managers dropped 3.1% in the worst 5-day stretch since December 2023.

bullets.title: Iran-US ceasefire removes acute energy tail risk; oil crashed >20% in Q2
bullets.body: The June 17 Iran-US MoU extended a 60-day ceasefire and reopened the Strait of Hormuz, removing the acute oil supply tail risk that had elevated energy prices since April. Brent fell from ~$120 in April to ~$70 by early July (20%+ decline in Q2), with US gasoline still 16-28% above pre-conflict levels given refinery lag. JPM cut Brent to $75 for 2H26 and 2027. Lower oil is now viewed as a meaningful tailwind to consumer spending and core inflation deceleration.

bullets.title: Comcast spins off NBCUniversal/Sky; CHTR in SpaceX mobile talks—cable sector M&A wave begins
bullets.body: Comcast announced a tax-free spin-off of NBCUniversal and Sky (~$60B revenue each) into a separate public company in ~12 months. CMCSA surged +22% intraday. Separately, Charter held exec-level talks with SpaceX on a consumer mobile phone partnership, sending CHTR +22%. Analysts (Citi, Wolfe) see the Comcast split as a precursor to a CMCSA/CHTR cable merger and potential NBCU sale to Netflix or Amazon. Comcast suspended buybacks to preserve investment-grade ratings.

bullets.title: Samsung/$SK Hynix announce $3.1T Korea mega-investment plan; AI capex super-cycle thesis reinforced
bullets.body: Samsung (W2.45tn) and SK Hynix (W1.1tn) announced massive multi-decade semiconductor investment programs through 2040, including a new Jeonnam-Gwangju chip cluster and an acceleration of the Yongin DRAM ramp by 12 years. This is bullish for semiconductor capital equipment (ASML, LRCX, AMAT) and upstream materials. UBS maintained Buy ratings on all major WFE names. SK Hynix also removed price caps from long-term supply contracts, enabling spot price pass-through.

bullets.title: Eurozone recovery underway; JPM raises growth forecasts, ECB likely hikes once more in September
bullets.body: The Euro area composite PMI was revised up to 50.0 in June, with Spain at 53.3 and Italy at 50.8. JPMorgan raised 4Q26-2Q27 GDP growth to 1.5% annualized (from 1.3%) as oil price declines improve household real income. Eurozone headline inflation fell to 2.8% YoY in June on energy drag; core declined to 2.4%. ECB President Lagarde retained a clear hawkish bias at Sintra, and JPM expects one final 25bp hike in September. Germany announced 33 reform proposals covering taxes, labor, and industrial policy.

bullets.title: Debasement trade roaring: gold correlated to real yields; JPM cuts gold targets but stays bullish 2027
bullets.body: Warsh's hawkish-but-data-dependent stance at Sintra and the soft NFP together reignited the 'debasement trade' (gold+, dollar−, curve steeper). Gold fell 12.1% in June—worst month since June 2013—on Fed hawkishness, but JPM's base case remains range-bound near-term ($4,300-$4,500/oz in 3Q-4Q26) with long-term bullish targets of $5,000/oz for 4Q27. Silver −21% and Bitcoin −19% in June were also notable. Dollar (DXY) +2.3% in June weighed on EM FX (−2.3%).

bullets.title: Regional banks benefit from 'hawkish hold': KRE up 15% since March on NII and loan growth
bullets.body: The combination of a hawkish Fed stance without immediate rate action has been ideal for regional banks—belly yields rise, funding costs stay muted, and loan growth accelerates. 22V and others prefer USB and FITB, downgrading RF on margin headwinds. RBC is bullish on US banks broadly on loan growth, NII acceleration, M&A momentum, and Basel III endgame. The key threshold to watch: core PCE above 0.21% MoM would tighten financial conditions and hurt the trade.

bullets.title: US lodging RevPAR surging +9.6% YoY; World Cup adding ~290bp across host markets
bullets.body: STR data for the week ending June 27 showed US RevPAR up 9.6% YoY (ADR +9.2%, occupancy +30bp), with luxury up 20.7% and Miami +52%, Las Vegas +24%, San Francisco +41%. The World Cup contributed approximately 290bp to the headline print. Trailing 28-day RevPAR was +8.0% YoY. European RevPAR also accelerated to +4.9% YoY. Both HLT and MAR are tracking above consensus for 2Q.

bullets.title: EM equity outflows at worst non-ETF pace since August 2015; Korea -$95.8B YTD
bullets.body: EM equity funds saw -$6.0bn weekly outflows, with non-ETF outflows of -$5.2bn—the worst since August 2015. Korea accelerated to -$11.7bn weekly (-$95.8bn YTD cumulative), with memory stocks hitting mandate limits for 10%+ of EM investors. Taiwan outflows also picked up. India sustained a third consecutive week of inflows (+$217mn). Year-to-date EM net flows remain positive at +$52bn, entirely driven by ETFs (+$82bn) masking -$30bn non-ETF redemptions.

bullets.title: China AI stocks to reassert leadership in August; tactical rotation continues in July
bullets.body: JPM's China equity strategy sees the A-share semiconductor/hardware correction (−8-9% vs CSI300's −3%) as driven by pre-Politburo meeting rotation, not fundamental weakness. The firm expects China AI (Zhongji Innolight, NAURA, Baidu) to reclaim leadership in August earnings season on strong 2Q results. MSCI China end-2026 base case: 100; CSI-300: 5,200. Tencent at −2SD on FTM P/E and Alibaba −22% in June are cited as accumulation opportunities.

bullets.title: China structural growth soft but tech manufacturing holds; JPM forecasts 4.7% full-year GDP
bullets.body: China domestic demand softened in 2Q after strong 1Q. Housing will not stabilize in 2026 due to unsold inventory and buyer confidence deficits. High-tech manufacturing rose 15.1% YoY in May, contributing ~40% of industrial growth. CPI inflation subdued at 1.2% in May; deflation risks could re-emerge in 2H. JPM expects 3.5% q/q saar in 3Q and 3.7% in 4Q, leaving full-year near 4.7% within the government's 4.5-5% target.

bullets.title: Tariff regime shifting to durable Section 301/232 framework; statutory rate converging to 9-10%
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes Section 122 tariffs expire July 24; July 7 Section 301 hearings are the key procedural catalyst. The statutory effective tariff rate is estimated at 9-10% with less dispersion than the original IEEPA regime. USMCA moved to annual reviews through 2036 rather than the 16-year extension that was expected; the US is demanding trade deficit reduction, tighter auto content rules (50% US-specific), and prevention of Asian transshipment through Mexico. Pharmaceutical tariffs are modeled at 15%.

bullets.title: IPO volumes at record $250B+ YTD; SpaceX $86B IPO is largest in history; AI infrastructure driving issuance
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs flags $129B in US IPOs YTD (7x YoY), dominated by the AI supercycle. SpaceX's $86.26bn IPO nearly tripled the prior record (Saudi Aramco's $29bn). June IPOs averaged +13.1% from pricing. Anthropic hired Goldman and Morgan Stanley for an IPO at ~$1.67T valuation; OpenAI is leaning toward 2027. The looming risk: twelve-figure lockup expirations—including $850bn HK$ (~$108bn) of China tech shares hitting Q3—could overwhelm demand if sentiment cools.
